handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

p.ref: Émile Chatelain, Paléographie des classiques latins II, plate XCI notice, PDF fifth page (zero-based 4): surviving Amores 3.12.26 followed by 3.14.3; used for coverage corroboration, not verse text.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of the 48 surviving canonical positions 3–50, including local source illegibility. The missing opening positions 1–2 are a source-confirmed gap, not verse containers; their old overlapping rectangles remain provenance only. Every surviving source position and evidence note has received an independent second reading.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l is a surviving canonical verse position3–50; blackened positions use illegibility gaps without claiming recoverable words. Opening positions 1–2 are not transmitted, corroborated by full-page source inspection and Chatelain’s manuscript description. Saved rectangles 1–2 remain unused facsimile provenance. Other zones are unchanged. Couplets are editorial grouping. Only source-supported visible line offsets carry indent; none is assigned automatically from parity. Mixed-content word boundaries contain no formatting newlines.

interpretation.p: Every evidence note has an independent disposition in the companion ledger. Documented image uncertainty remains local and is not a human-review assignment.

revisionDesc.change: Independently inspected full images 97–99, every surviving position 3–50 in enlarged strips, all 42 notes and targeted details. Corrected limited source fragments and uncertainty, confirmed source indentation and opening absence against Chatelain. Original zones remain unchanged.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

gap.desc: Canonical positions 1–2 are not transmitted at the source discontinuity. Full images 97–98 and Chatelain’s plate XCI notice establish resumption at 3.14.3. Their saved overlapping annotation rectangles are retained only as provenance and do not establish additional written verses.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: Full images 97–98 and the direct Chatelain manuscript description independently confirm resumption at 3.14.3 after the lacuna. Opening 1–2 are not transmitted; the two overlapping original rectangles remain unused provenance. The reference is plate XCI notice 1, printed introductory II,1, PDF fifth page (zero-based 4). No original leaf count or historical cause is inferred.
The annotated opening surviving position remains wholly blackened. No defensible letters or indent can be recovered from the full page and enlarged upper strip.
The second surviving position is obscured throughout its assigned row. The full-line illegibility gap and unchanged source zone remain appropriate.
The assigned row is blackened; no complete defensible word is established by the enlarged source. Its gap is retained.
The lower edge of the upper stain permits the tentative group famosam. The rest remains obscured; no wording is reconstructed.
The tentative group que nocte latent is compatible with the surviving pale strokes. Surrounding text remains masked by blackening.
Clam facias facta referre can be followed in the photograph; the pale opening Et que and final palam remain qualified.
The central terra corpus iunctura quiriti is supported by the source. Ignoto remains pale and qualified. The unusual terra is not replaced from an edition.
The leftmost Nonne sit is faint and less secure than the first pass claimed. It is now explicitly unclear. Populum mouit ante fera is visible; no alternative opening is supplied.
The enlarged middle row supports profiteris, including its terminal sequence; the former uncertainty is removed. The surrounding source wording Tu que and fame peccata sinistre remains unchanged.
The opening doubled-minim sequence remains compatible with tentative Commisi. Its uncertainty is retained; perages indiciumque tui can be followed.
Si tibi mens melior saltemue imitare pudicas is visible, including saltemue and imitare. No normalized substitution is warranted.
The clearly written non eris is preserved in the full row Teque probam quamuis non eris esse putem.
The pale initial group Que facis hec facito remains qualified. Tantum fecisse negato is legible.
A dark spot interrupts the coram region. The provisional letters remain local uncertainty; the mark does not establish deletion or an earlier textual state.
The middle minim sequence in nequitiam is less distinct than adjacent Est qui and locus exigat omnibus illum. The original local qualification remains justified.

The enlarged row visibly continues after inple with a t-shaped stroke and rounded final o before procul. The tentative group is corrected to Deliciis inpleto; the rest procul inde pudor remains clear.
The source has the compact et ligature after Absit. Its declared schematic glyph and expansion preserve the written form and defensible meaning.
The source sequence Inque modos uenerem mille figuret amor is readable, with manuscript spelling unchanged.
The pale row Illic nec uoces nec uerba iuuantia cessent remains legible in enlarged context. No modern punctuation is inserted.
The source supports Indue cum tunicis metuentem crimina uultum in the lower-page enlargement, despite weaker initial ink.
The last row on image 98 supports Et liceat stulta credulitate frui. The next full photograph begins the canonical 31–50 portion.
The top left-page stain on image 99 obscures this assigned row. A whole-line illegibility gap is retained without assumed initial, indent or punctuation.
No defensible continuous reading emerges from the second blackened row. The original zone and whole-line gap remain unchanged.
Only the right-hand capillos is tentatively distinguishable beneath the darkening. No complete opening is supplied.
Habere notam is readable to the right of the diagonal obstruction. Earlier strokes remain too merged with damage for a reliable word sequence.
The oculos group remains tentative within the mottled row. The diagonal intrusion is not encoded as a scribal cancellation.
The final mihi remains tentative; the preceding writing is too entangled with stain and crossing strokes for a defensible reconstruction.
Peccasse fateris remains a qualified terminal group. Additional preceding strokes are visible but do not warrant an expanded continuous transcription.
Perque meos artus frigida gutta fluit can be followed below the darkest portion. Its actual inset is visible in full-page context.

The enlarged F-like lexical T at the opening is visible, followed by unc amo tunc odi frustra quod amare necesse est. Large-initial markup is retained without inventing a correcting hand or overwritten letter.
The row supports Tunc ego sed tecum mortuus esse uelim in this order. Its inset is source-supported.

The weak equidem inquiram region and unusual terminal turpabis remain uncertain on direct enlargement. The darker stroke near the terminal opening does not justify reconstructing an earlier letter or removing the qualification.
Lisque is followed by a pale incomplete span. Falsi muneris instar erit remains readable; the intervening gap is retained.
Before deprensa tenebere culpa, the enlarged photograph supports tentative manifesta. That fragment is added after the remaining initial gap; a complete opening is not reconstructed.
The beginning Et fuerint remains weak and qualified. Oculis probra uidenda meis can be followed in the photograph.
The surviving uisa mihi fuerint group and tentative Que and bene uisa negato are retained. The initial interruption remains a gap.
The right-hand sequence separates as lumina followed by tentative nostra tuis, not the first-pass nostris. Concedant remains qualified and the intervening text remains a gap.
Prona and uincere are faint but compatible with the source. No further wording is added from the weak surrounding strokes.
Et modo non and terminal amor remain tentative. The pale middle is not reconstructed.
The final lower portion is very faint and partly darkened. Only tentative Cum is retained rather than completing the row from familiar wording.
After visible Et, the enlargement supports tentative lingua before the stain. This limited fragment is added; the remaining text stays illegible. The following large Q belongs to 3.15.
